subject: BlueHarbor tenancy & throughput synthesis — post-call summary and ops asks
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <m.singh@blueharbortx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: tenancy options, throughput targets, and next steps (BlueHarbor)

Maya — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and a clear ops path. Key points below (short bullets + asks). I attached my raw call notes and the initial sizing worksheet for your review.

Customer pain & goals:
- Current model serving is hitting unpredictable latency during nightly batch windows; business impact: delayed clinical inference results and slower product iteration.
- Must meet PHI handling requirements (HIPAA) and isolate dev/staging from production.
- Business target: support ~10k inference requests/day with 50 RPS peak, anticipate burst to 120 RPS during morning ingest.
- p99 latency target: <= 200ms for 95% of inference types; non-critical batch jobs can run asynchronously.

Isolation & tenancy constraints:
- Prefer a dedicated tenancy per product team (logical isolation + VPC peering).
- Encryption at rest + customer-managed KMS is required.
- Disaster recovery: want ability to failover to a secondary region (EU or US-east) within 30 minutes.

Throughput & scaling asks:
- Expected growth: 2–3x throughput over next 12 months.
- Query distribution: ~70% short (<128 tokens), 30% long (128–1024 tokens).

Commercial and timeline:
- Procurement window: evaluating reserved pool for Q4 start; preference for a 12-month commit if SLA and isolation controls are validated.
- Cost sensitivity: want an estimate of committed vs burst pricing and expected cost per 1M tokens.

Immediate next steps (action items):
1) Ben / SE: schedule a 60–90m technical deep-dive to validate peak RPS, KV cache sizing, and model replica counts.
2) Karthik (me): share a draft SLO matrix and two tenancy proposals (single-tenant reserved pool vs tenant-isolated reserved slots) by EOD tomorrow.
3) BlueHarbor: confirm whether DR region must be EU or if US-east is acceptable for now.
4) BlueHarbor procurement: share any standard PO/contract constraints and target procurement date.

Attachments: blueharbor-call-notes.pdf (raw notes), initial-sizing.xlsx (rough GPU/replica sizing).

If any of the numbers above are off, flag them and I’ll update. Planning to put together a short ops playbook for the deep-dive.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Maya Singh <m.singh@blueharbortx.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, procurement@blueharbortx.com
Date: 2026-08-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: tenancy options, throughput targets, and next steps (BlueHarbor)

Thanks for the clear summary — very helpful. A few clarifications and confirmations from our side:

Confirmations:
- The traffic mix and peak RPS numbers look right based on our monitoring. 50 RPS steady, 120 RPS peak is accurate for the first phase.
- We absolutely need customer-managed KMS and VPC isolation between prod and non-prod; regulatory requires that segmentation for PHI workflows.

Clarifications / asks:
- DR region: for now we prefer US-east for DR to keep latency predictable, but may require EU in phase 2. Can you include both options in the SLO doc?
- Security evidence: please provide a short checklist we can hand to our InfoSec (SOC 2 in-scope items, encryption details, key rotation cadence).
- SLA question: we need clarity on what Redwood’s automatic fallback looks like if a reserved pool degrades — is there a hosted fallback, and how does that interact with data residency constraints?

Procurement:
- We are targeting contract signing in early Q4; procurement will need an itemized estimate and a standard contract template. I’m looping procurement on this thread.

Attachments: I’ve attached our security checklist with a few extra items (blueharbor-security-checklist.pdf) — please review and mark which items are covered by Redwood by default vs. need a control design conversation.

Happy to hop on another call; Ben, can you set up the SE deep-dive next week (week of Aug 9)?

Best,
Maya
Maya Singh
Director of ML Ops
BlueHarbor Therapeutics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: BlueHarbor qualification — recommended ops plan and owners

Ben / Stephanie — internal summary and proposed assignment following Maya’s reply. Please keep internal notes on required technical artifacts.

Quick synthesis:
- Requirement: dedicated/reserved GPUs with tenant isolation per product team; customer-managed KMS; VPC peering; DR to US-east (option for EU in phase 2).
- Target SLOs: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 200ms for online paths; 99.9% uptime for production endpoints; failover < 30 minutes.

Initial sizing (ballpark):
- Traffic mix suggests a modest fleet: 4 x H100-style instances for steady-state with autoscaling to 8 instances for peaks (model dependent). If we propose quantized LLM variants we may reduce to 3–5 smaller instances. See attached initial-sizing.xlsx.
- KV cache: persistent cache per tenancy recommended to keep p99 stable during morning bursts.

Operational proposals:
- Tenancy option A (recommended): reserved slots for BlueHarbor prod with dedicated GPU pool + VPC peering + KMS. Offer defined burst policy (additional shared burst capacity in same region) and an explicit hosted-fallback policy that is audited and requires customer opt-in for PHI (disabled by default).
- Tenancy option B: fully single-tenant cluster (higher cost) for strictest isolation; faster failover SLAs.

SE ask (Ben): run the deep-dive, validate per-model latency assumptions, confirm replica counts for the two common model sizes they mentioned in the call, and surface any hidden throughput constraints (disk I/O, KV hot keys).
Legal / Procurement ask (Stephanie): prepare a draft term sheet with standard 12-month reserved pricing + burst schedule; include optional addendum for EU DR.

Deliverables & owners:
- Karthik: publish SLO matrix and two tenancy proposals to the Drive link (see related_links) by EOD tomorrow.
- Ben: schedule deep-dive (90m) with BlueHarbor for week of Aug 9; include an ops rundown and a short runbook template.
- Stephanie: draft commercial term sheet and list of legal exceptions needed for PHI handling.

I’ll capture this into HubSpot under deal BH-2026-0842 and move to "Qualified — SE review".

--
Karthik
